subject: Compensation bucketing + local index guidance for offers
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Compensation bucketing + local index guidance for offers

Team —

We need to finalize the comp band definitions and the local indexing rules for offers before next week's hiring committee. Key asks:

- Agree on the bucketing scheme for L4/L5/L6 (we currently have 5 salary buckets per level; propose consolidating to 3 offer bands: lower/mid/upper).
- Define geo multipliers for high-cost cities (SF/NY/LDN) vs. regional markets; propose a market index table.
- Decide when to apply percentile vs. bucket-based offers for candidate improvements (example: exceptional IC candidate vs. lateral hire).

Attached is comp_bands_draft_v2.xlsx with: current anchors, proposed 3-band mapping, and a sample offer matrix. Please review the 'Local Index' tab — I added a preliminary multiplier column based on salary survey snapshots.

Constraints to keep in mind: payroll timing for promotions (Jan run), finance needs to see the impact on run-rate, and our total comp guardrails for offers beyond midpoint.

Can Neha and Laura weight in with benchmarking and legal/ops flags? I'd like a short decision matrix by EOD Monday so I can present to hiring committee on Tues. If there are outstanding vendor numbers, loop them in.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

Attachments: comp_bands_draft_v2.xlsx (Excel, 48 KB)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compensation bucketing + local index guidance for offers

Thanks Marcus — good framing. Quick notes from benchmarking and recommended next steps:

Summary of recommended approach
- Keep 3 offer buckets per level (lower/mid/upper) but add a 'stretch' discretionary band for critical hires (with CFO sign-off).
- Use percentile anchoring for base salary (25/50/75) and then apply a market multiplier per city. For total comp we should consider equity uplift for mid/upper buckets.

Geo multipliers (proposed)
- SF Bay Area: 1.20
- New York City: 1.15
- London: 1.10
- Other major metro (Seattle, Boston, Toronto): 1.08
- Rest-of-US: 1.00

Data sources and caveats
- I ran a quick pass against Northbridge's Q4 data and a recruiting-market CSV Greenleaf shared — summarized in market_benchmark_2026_Q4.csv (attached). These are 90-day snapshots and understate bonuses for sales/CS.
- For remote candidates who remain in high-cost jurisdictions we should default to the physical work location for multiplier decisions; exceptions require manager + comp sign-off.

Operational asks
- Laura: can you check if payroll/legal needs different phrasing for UK offers (pension calculations + benefits)?
- Aditya: please model the Jan run-rate impact for a +10 headcount ramp in the infra org using the proposed multipliers.

If the group agrees, I suggest we publish the 'Offer Matrix v1' to the Confluence page and include a short FAQ for recruiters.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Head of Total Rewards
Redwood Inference

Attachments: market_benchmark_2026_Q4.csv (CSV, 127 KB)
From: Sarah Williams <sarah@northbridgevc.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Northbridge Q4 comp benchmark report (for Redwood)

Hi Neha / Marcus —

Attached is the Northbridge abbreviated bench report you requested. Key takeaways for FY27 planning:

- Market medians moved up ~3.2% year-over-year with stronger movement for senior ICs in infra and modelops.
- Equity velocity accelerated at startups with heavy hiring; benchmarks suggest offering equity +7% vs. last year for 'upper' bands to remain competitive.
- Regional variation is material; our London index is closer to Seattle than SF (we include currency adjustments).

I've flagged the rows where sample size < 10 so you can treat those as directional. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to walk through the sheets.

Best,
Sarah Williams
Senior People Insights Analyst
Northbridge VC

Attachments: northbridge_bench_report.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Compensation bucketing + local index guidance for offers

Thanks for the fast turn. Recap and recommended decision path for the hiring committee:

Decisions I will propose Tuesday
- Adopt 3 offer buckets per level with a documented 'stretch' band requiring CFO approval.
- Apply the geo multipliers Neha proposed and bake them into the offer tool so recruiters see adjusted anchor ranges in-screen.
- Use percentile anchoring (25/50/75) for base and include guidance for equity uplift (Northbridge recommends +7% for 'upper' band).

Action items
- Neha: finalize the Market Index table and mark any low-sample rows in the Drive doc (due EOD Monday).
- Aditya: run the headcount cost model with +10 hires across infra and ops for the Jan payroll run (due Monday COB).
- Laura: draft the UK/EMEA phrasing for offers and pensions to include in the FAQ (due Tuesday morning).
- Evelyn: confirm hiring committee time and I will send the agenda.

I'll attach the final workbook to the committee packet after Neha's update. If anyone has a strong objection to the multipliers, flag now — otherwise I'll proceed with the committee ask.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference

CC: Greenleaf Recruiting <offers@greenleaf.com>
